title: Composition and Surface Termination Control Band Alignments in P3HT/Perovskite Heterostructures
abstract: Hybrid organic-inorganic perovskite heterostructures are emerging platforms for energy conversion and optoelectronic devices, yet the effects of composition and surface terminations on band alignment remain poorly understood. Here, using high-throughput first-principles calculations, we systematically reveal the effect of composition and surface termination on the band alignment of 820 heterostructures formed between poly(3-hexylthiophene) (P3HT) variants and conventional and mixed-cation metal halide perovskites. Band edge analysis predicts concentration dependent band alignments, with most Pb and Sn based perovskites exhibiting Type II and III behavior while mixed-cation CsMASnBr3 uniquely forms Type-I junctions with all P3HT variants. Explicit interface calculations reveal that surface termination can reverse the predicted alignment in conventional tin perovskites, while the mixed cation perovskite preserves Type-I alignment with P3HT regardless of termination. Despite negligible charge transfer, termination dependent band offsets produce markedly different carrier confinement, establishing design principles for engineering P3HT/perovskite interfaces.
summary: This work uses first-principles calculations to map the band alignment in P3HT/perovskite heterostructures, revealing that surface termination and cation mixing are critical design parameters. The findings establish that mixed-cation perovskites can maintain a desirable Type-I alignment, offering new principles for engineering organic-inorganic interfaces for energy applications.
main_problem: The study aims to understand how the chemical composition and surface termination of metal halide perovskites influence the band alignment when forming heterostructures with P3HT polymers.
main_result: The mixed-cation perovskite CsMASnBr3 uniquely forms a Type-I band alignment with P3HT regardless of surface termination, whereas pure Sn-based perovskites show termination-dependent alignment changes.
method: The research employs high-throughput first-principles calculations using DFT (PBE functional with DFT-D3 corrections) and HSE06 for electronic structure analysis.
model_or_system: The system modeled is the interface between P3HT variants and various metal halide perovskites (conventional and mixed-cation). Calculations are performed on slab models to simulate different surface terminations.
key_observables: Band alignment type (Type-I, II, III), Valence Band Maximum (VBM), Conduction Band Minimum (CBM), and band offsets ($\Delta	ext{CBM}$, $\Delta	ext{VBM}$).
important_parameters: Composition (e.g., CsMASnBr3 vs. CsSnBr3), surface termination ($	ext{AX}$ vs. $	ext{BX}$), and the polymer type (P3HT variants).
main_assumptions: The primary assumption is that band alignment is governed by orbital coupling and carrier confinement rather than significant net charge transfer, although the dependence on termination is highly sensitive.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate crystal structures, band alignment heatmaps for 820 heterostructures, and detailed projected band structures comparing different terminations for specific Sn-based perovskite/P3HT interfaces.
paper_structure: The paper systematically analyzes the effect of composition and termination on band alignment using high-throughput calculations, contrasting the behavior of pure vs. mixed-cation perovskites, and detailing the mechanism of band offset formation.
why_interesting: While focused on solid-state optoelectronics, the rigorous application of first-principles methods to map out complex, tunable interfacial electronic states (band alignment) is relevant to understanding engineered quantum interfaces in general.
